module: Small ImGui and string utility functions shared by the sections of the Dynamic Decals tool: centered text, image preview with its size, image or icon tooltip, formatting of camelCase names. Useful to a modder writing a section or a widget for this tool.
notes: splitAndCapitalizeCamelCase and capitalizeWords return two values (gsub returns the string and the number of replacements); wrap the call in parentheses to keep only the string.
imageWidget and imageTooltip go through editor.getTempTextureObj(path); a "/" path (missing texture) is displayed as a square.

textUnformattedCentered.desc: Displays plain text horizontally centered in the available area. Does nothing if the text is nil.

textColoredCentered.desc: Like textUnformattedCentered but with an ImGui color.

imageWidget.desc: Displays an image (tinted with the editor's BeamNG color) at the given width keeping the ratio, followed by its size "W x H".

overrideWidth.desc: Width in pixels; default is the full available width.

imageTooltip.desc: If the previous ImGui item is hovered, displays a tooltip with the image and its size. Default width: preference `dynamicDecalsTool.imageTooltip.texturePreviewSize`.

iconTooltip.desc: Draws an "info" icon with a tooltip containing the message.

inline.desc: If true, places the icon on the same line as the previous item.

splitAndCapitalizeCamelCase.desc: Turns a camelCase string into space-separated words with an initial capital (e.g. "brushStroke" gives "Brush Stroke").

returns.desc: Formatted string (followed by the number of substitutions of the last gsub).

capitalizeWords.desc: Capitalizes the first letter of each word and lowercases the rest.

returns.desc: Formatted string (followed by the number of substitutions).

registerEditorPreferences.desc: Registers the float preference `dynamicDecalsTool.imageTooltip.texturePreviewSize` (default 128, from 32 to 512).

editorPreferenceValueChanged.desc: Hook called when a preference changes. Does nothing here.

setup.desc: Called by the tool: stores the reference to the tool (required for iconTooltip, which uses tool.getIconSize()).
